In [[Group theory#Finite group theory|finite group theory]], a [[mathematics|mathematical]] discipline, the '''Gilman–Griess theorem''', [[mathematical proof|proved]] by Robert H. Gilman and [[Robert Griess|Robert L. Griess]], classifies the [[finite simple group]]s of [[characteristic 2 type]] with ''e''(''G'')&nbsp;≥&nbsp;4 that have a "standard component", which covers one of the three cases of the [[trichotomy theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Gilman | first1=Robert H. | last2=Griess | first2=Robert L. | author2-link=Robert Griess | title=Finite groups with standard components of Lie type over fields of characteristic two | doi=10.1016/0021-8693(83)90007-8 | mr=691810 | year=1983 | journal=[[Journal of Algebra]] | issn=0021-8693 | volume=80 | issue=2 | pages=383–516| url=https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/bitstream/2027.42/25314/1/0000759.pdf | hdl=2027.42/25314 | hdl-access=free }}</ref>
